hints: At constant speed on level ground, driving force equals total resistance: $F_D = 300 + 100 = 400\text{ N}$.
Apply the power formula $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
At constant speed on horizontal ground, acceleration is zero, so the engine's driving force balances the total resistance on both vehicles:
$$F_D = F_{\text{res, van}} + F_{\text{res, trailer}} = 300 + 100 = 400\text{ N}$$

Use the formula for power:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute $F_D = 400\text{ N}$ and $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 400 \times 25 = 10000\text{ W} = 10\text{ kW}$$

hints: Consider the trailer separately moving at constant speed: acceleration is zero.
The forward tension in the cable must balance the trailer's resistance force of $100\text{ N}$.
walkthrough: Isolate the trailer of mass $500\text{ kg}$. It travels at constant speed, so its acceleration is zero ($a = 0$).

The only horizontal forces acting on the trailer are the forward pull of tension $T$ and the backward resistance of $100\text{ N}$:
$$T - F_{\text{resistance}} = 0$$
$$T = 100\text{ N}$$

hints: Find the driving force from power $25\text{ kW}$ and speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F_D = \frac{25000}{20} = 1250\text{ N}$.
Write the equation of motion for the trailer: $T - 100 - 500g\sin 4^\circ = 500a$.
Write the equation of motion for the van: $1250 - 300 - T - 3000g\sin 4^\circ = 3000a$.
Eliminate acceleration $a$ by equating $6 \times$ the trailer equation to the van equation, observing that the gravity terms cancel out completely.
walkthrough:
First, calculate the forward driving force $F_D$ exerted by the van's engine at the given instant:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{25000}{20} = 1250\text{ N}$$
Next, set up the equations of motion along the $4^\circ$ slope for both vehicles using $F_{\text{net}} = ma$.

For the trailer of mass $500\text{ kg}$:
$$T - 100 - 500g\sin 4^\circ = 500a \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

For the van of mass $3000\text{ kg}$:
$$1250 - 300 - T - 3000g\sin 4^\circ = 3000a$$
$$950 - T - 3000g\sin 4^\circ = 3000a \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

To eliminate the acceleration $a$, multiply Equation 1 by $6$ so that both right-hand sides equal $3000a$:
$$6(T - 100 - 500g\sin 4^\circ) = 3000a$$
$$6T - 600 - 3000g\sin 4^\circ = 3000a$$

Equate this expression to Equation 2:
$$6T - 600 - 3000g\sin 4^\circ = 950 - T - 3000g\sin 4^\circ$$

Add $3000g\sin 4^\circ$ to both sides to cancel the gravitational component:
$$6T - 600 = 950 - T$$

Add $T$ to both sides and add $600$ to both sides:
$$7T = 1550$$
$$T = \frac{1550}{7} \approx 221.43\text{ N} \approx 221\text{ N}$$
